lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD hammer prices at Gowans, Hobart (premium extra), none unsold, none asking. Six mixed boxes of Tasmanian ephemera made $9 to $60 hammer, mostly $40 to $55. Category outliers run to $80 and $190 (two boxes). AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: No maximum set. The Gowans boxes are sold and recent, but their photos show mostly 1970s to 2000s booklets and programmes, while this box is older printed flyers, receipts and tickets, so none is the same item in similar condition. If you treated them as same item anyway: lowest $9 / 1.22 = 7.38, keep max $5; using the typical $40 hammer, $40 / 1.22 = 32.79, so about $30. Flip: likely resale about $40 less roughly 15% selling fees and $15 postage = $19, / 2.44 = 7.79, so $5. Not worth flipping.
lots.confidence_reason: Contents read clearly in the photos, but no sold comparable with matching contents. Mixed-box comparables only. WebSearch cap reached, so Armitage's own past results were not checked.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All 10 researcher Gowans entries confirmed against the API (ids, cents, bid counts and dates match). Relabelled same_item: the boxes stay 'close' as lot type only, flagged as different contents after checking Gowans photos. Rowallan identification corrected to Lady Bastyan.
lots.key_photo_findings: Invitation card reads 'His Excellency The Governor and Lady Bastyan', handwritten to Mrs W.F. Ellis (Governor Bastyan, 1968-73). Herd & Co (1920) Ltd receipt dated 1929. Rowitta flyer, Derby Day flyer (Mr Charles Woods, Miss Gertrude Darley), Cox & Webb 'Mercery of Merit', 1954 Royal Visit pink admission tickets, TAA ticket jackets, F & G Furniture Auctions receipt, Launceston Homoeopathic Hospital letter, photographic postcard of a house.
lots.condition: Aged paper, toning, some creases, edge tears and old tape on the larger sheets. Box contents only partly visible.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there anything underneath the top layer (photographs, postcards, pre-1920 items or stamps on covers), or is it all receipts, flyers and tickets like the photos?

lots.what_it_is: Two navy Montblanc leather pieces in Montblanc boxes with dust bags: a smooth leather bifold wallet with the white star emblem, and a textured (Saffiano style) vertical card holder with the star. The wallet looks like Meisterstueck leather; the card holder texture looks more like the Sartorial line. Exact models and authenticity not confirmed.

asking.note: Page opened. Wallet 6cc in Meisterstueck Leather, new. Exact model match to the lot wallet not confirmed. Used items sell well below retail, so this is a ceiling only. AUD, no conversion.

Page opened. Card Holder 4cc in Sartorial Leather, new. The lot card holder looks like textured leather; model not confirmed. Same page lists Card Holder 6cc in Meisterstueck Leather at AU$ 500 and Card Holder 5cc in Extreme Leather at AU$ 460.

lots.guide_summary: Only ASKING evidence: current new retail in Australia, AU$ 460 to AU$ 580 for card holders and AU$ 810 for a Meisterstueck 6cc wallet. No sold or unsold results found. Pre-owned prices are typically a fraction of retail, so real value is well below this range.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so no maximum bid. Retail new totals about AU$ 1,300 for the pair, but that is an asking price for new goods and cannot set a bid.
lots.confidence_reason: Asking (new retail) evidence only, single photo, model codes and authenticity unread, WebSearch cap reached so no pre-owned sale results were found.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher returned no entries. Added two ASKING entries from the Montblanc AU site (page opened). Gowans API checked for montblanc: only a pen lot (id 417826), not used. Grays search returned no Montblanc wallets.
lots.key_photo_findings: Montblanc boxes and dust bags present, star emblems on both pieces. Wallet leather shows light creasing and some surface marks, suggesting use. Card holder has a pebbled or cross-grain texture, different from the smooth wallet. No serial or style number visible.
lots.condition: Appears used but tidy. Boxes present, outer box a little scuffed.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you read the style or serial number inside each piece (and on the box labels), and do the boxes include the Montblanc warranty or service cards? How worn are the edges and inside the wallet?

lots.what_it_is: A.W. Kappel and W. Egmont Kirby, British and European Butterflies and Moths (Macrolepidoptera), with 30 coloured plates by H. Deuchert and S. Blocombe. Title page imprint reads London: Ernest Nister, New York: E.P. Dutton & Co, Printed in Bavaria, so the c.1895-96 first issue. Pictorial gilt and silver cloth.
